Anika / Kimberly / Ben — attaching the artifacts for your review. Summary notes below; see attached PDFs for annotated visuals.

Attachments included: inference-dataflow-v3.pdf, threat-summary-annotated.pdf

Technical summary (high level):
- Control plane: Redwood control plane is a multi-tenant control plane that manages orchestration, model catalog, and billing. For Private deployments we offer a customer-managed control plane option where the control APIs are proxied through a customer VPC via PrivateLink. Control plane traffic is authenticated with mTLS and RBAC-bound tokens.

- Data plane (inference): Model execution occurs in one of three modes: Hosted (Redwood-managed GPU pools), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools for the customer), or Private (customer VPC / on-prem nodes with sidecars). In Hosted/Dedicated the data plane runs in Redwood VPCs with strict egress controls; for Private the data plane lives inside the customer boundary.

- KV cache & model artifacts: KV cache is memory-resident in the serving runtime; cached prefixes are kept in-system and never written to persistent shared storage unless configured for replication. Model artifacts (weights) are stored in encrypted blob storage with customer or Redwood-managed KMS. Access to model artifacts is limited by service identity and short-lived tokens.

- Networking & egress: Default deployments use VPC egress allowlists and NAT gateway controls. For customers with stricter needs we recommend VPC peering or PrivateLink and a locked-down egress bastion. We also support per-tenant egress policies and prefix-based routing to minimize lateral exposure.

- Threat highlights and mitigations (brief):
  * Egress misconfiguration: enforce egress allowlist + per-tenant policy + continuous SOC alerting.
  * KV cache exfil: in-memory cache, process-scoped; no default remote persistence, strong process isolation and sidecar-level least privilege.
  * Model poisoning during onboarding: signed model artifacts + code signing + ingestion quarantines + test/validation suites.
  * Control plane impersonation: mTLS + short-lived tokens + audit logging + anomaly detection on API patterns.

If helpful, we can provide a variant of the diagram that overlays your expected operator roles and network ranges.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
